body.statement:
Put \(D=Sd\).  For every fixed nonempty class with a compatible donor envelope \(B\ge D^2\), fixed \(d\), and fixed \(\lambda\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,T},P_{1,T})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
with the declared marginal design-density bounds and geometric conditional beta-mixing envelope such that
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
The event means are stable given the complete historical design, the historical errors are centered given that design, and both laws satisfy the maintained two-sided local modulus.  The donor marginal is common to the two laws and may be chosen so that \(\Sigma=I_D\) and the standardized fourth moment is exactly \(D^2\), including when \(B=D^2\).  Consequently the spacing contribution to conditional minimax mean squared error is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), and every uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest interval has worst-case expected length at least \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  Hence the logarithm in the uniform geometric-mixing spacing term is unavoidable without an additional anti-clustering restriction.  When \(B<D^2\), the class is empty and no substantive minimax assertion is made.
body.justification: The explicit rare-block design array certifies the uniform logarithm for every compatible envelope, including \(B=D^2\).
body.gap: Marginal density and geometric design mixing allow local states to occur in blocks of logarithmic length; the common donor marginal has covariance \(I_D\) and fourth moment \(D^2\).
body.consumer: The iid spacing expression remains only a stricter-design comparator, and the boundary converse retains the spacing channel.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(D=Sd\).  For any member of the class, define \(Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0)\).  The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\) and \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity} imply \(\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Therefore, by taking traces, applying Jensen's inequality, and then using \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment},
\[
D^2=\{\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]\}^2
\le\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\]
Thus \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix henceforth \(B\ge D^2\), an interior query, and one cohort having fixed positive weight; hold all remaining cohorts fixed across the two laws.  For sufficiently small fixed \(c_p,c_L>0\), let
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\).  Since \(p_T\asymp(\log T)/T\) whereas \(\rho_0^{L_T}\asymp T^{-c_L|\log\rho_0|}\), reducing \(c_p\) gives
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{16}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at the selected cohort block of \(z_0\), contained in \([0,1]^d\), and having Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  Its radius satisfies
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{17}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently across blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the selected cohort's design points independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  At each time the marginal density equals
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:design-density} holds because \(c_X\le1\le C_X\).  At lags at least \(L_T\), the relevant sigma-fields use independent block variables.  At smaller lags, only one shared block can create dependence.  Expanding the two-component mixture bounds its absolute-regularity distance from the product law by \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Since \(\rho_0^\ell\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(1\le\ell<L_T\), (16) implies
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}<L_T,\\
0,&\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}}.
\tag{19}
\]
This is precisely the design-only mixing condition.

Choose a bounded Holder carrier \(g\) lying in the interior of the response range.  Give it a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\) if \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there if \(0<\lambda\le1\); scale it inside the maintained two-sided modulus envelope.  With a fixed smooth bump \(\psi\), supported on the unit ball and satisfying \(\psi(0)=1\), put
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda
\psi\left(\frac{x-z_0}{h_T}\right).
\tag{20}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_b\), both surfaces remain in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and in the response interior.  If \(\lambda>1\), the bump increment over displacement \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\); it therefore cannot cancel the carrier's affine lower modulus.  If \(0<\lambda\le1\), its increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so it cannot cancel the cusp lower modulus when \(c_b\) is small.  The Holder upper bound gives the upper modulus.  Thus both laws satisfy \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Conditional on the complete design, draw bounded historical response paths independently across units from kernels having mean \(m_\ell(X_{st})\); kernels may vary by unit.  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of the design with a common mean under both laws, and complete untreated event potential outcomes so their cohort-average means are \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{21}
\]
For the donors use, under both laws, iid copies of
\[
Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\qquad
U_j\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\]
independently of the panel.  The calculation in (4) gives \(\Sigma=I_D\) and standardized fourth moment exactly \(D^2\le B\).  In particular, this donor completion remains valid at \(B=D^2\) and carries no information distinguishing the two spacing laws.  Take exact historical coordinates.  Define the potential outcomes by consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment, and make all potential outcomes invariant to other units' assignments.  Equations (18)--(21), the common donor calculation, and these completions verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  Since the number of blocks is \(T/L_T+O(1)\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{22}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), every selected-cohort design point lies outside \(A_T\), where the two surfaces in (20) agree.  The complete observed-data laws therefore coincide on this event, so
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{23}
\]
The observed event mean is common, whereas event transport changes the untreated event mean of the selected cohort by \(c_bh_T^\lambda\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (17) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{24}
\]
For the finitely many \(T\) preceding (16), use a fixed interior ball and two sufficiently close bounded response kernels with positive affinity and fixed nonzero target separation; decreasing the common constant makes (23)--(24) valid for all positive \(T\).

For any estimator, the two events on which its error from the respective target is at least half the separation cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure in (23) yields conditional squared risk at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  Reducing \(c_p\) makes (23) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\).  A conditionally honest interval covers both target values on overlap measure at least \(a_0\), and on that event its length is at least the separation in (24).  Its worst-case conditional expected length is therefore at least \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  This proves the claim for every compatible envelope without an anti-clustering premise.
